::: {.why}
The first strategy this year with two legs, a borrow cost and real turnover, and the first time the cost assumption is large enough to decide the answer.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Report the strategy's Sharpe before and after costs and state the turnover that separates them.
- Say what round-trip cost would take the strategy to zero, and whether that number is realistic.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Run the backtest over the trading period with the pairs and hedge ratios fixed by the formation-period screen. Apply your cost assumption on every rebalance. Report gross Sharpe, net Sharpe, annual turnover and the cost drag in basis points a year.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Find the break-even: sweep the round-trip cost from zero to 50 basis points and plot net Sharpe against it. Read off the cost at which the strategy stops working, and compare against what you would actually pay in a liquid US large cap. That single plot is more informative about the strategy than its Sharpe is.
:::
:::

## The running strategy

::: {.project}
The pairs strategy runs end to end with costs and produces a net Sharpe alongside a break-even cost curve. That curve becomes the standard chart for every strategy in the alpha book, because it says more than the headline number does.
:::
